verses.text: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
“He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
“About nine in the morning, he went out again and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
“He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and I’ll pay you whatever is fair.’ So they went.
“He went out again around noon and three in the afternoon and did the same.
“About five in the afternoon, he found more people standing there. He asked, ‘Why have you been standing here idle all day?’
“They said, ‘Nobody hired us.’ He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and I’ll pay you what’s fair.’
“When evening came, the vineyard owner told his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages. Start with the last ones hired and finish with the first.’
“The people hired around five came, and each received a denarius.
“When the first workers came, they expected to get more. But each of them also received a denarius.
“They took the money and complained to the landowner:
“‘These last workers did only one hour, but you paid them the same as us. We carried the day’s load and the scorching heat!’
“He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I’m not cheating you. Didn’t we agree on one denarius?
“‘Take your pay and go. I want to give the last worker the same as I gave you.
“‘Can’t I do what I want with what belongs to me? Are you jealous because I’m generous?’
“So the last will be first, and the first last. Many are called, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside. On the way, he told them:
“We’re going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes. They’ll condemn him to death
“and hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked, whipped, and crucified. On the third day he’ll be raised.”
Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt down and asked him for something.
He asked her, “What do you want?” She said, “Promise that my two sons can sit beside you in your Kingdom—one on your right, one on your left.”
Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you’re asking. Can you drink the cup I’m about to drink and be baptized with my baptism?” They said, “We can.”
He told them, “You will drink my cup and be baptized with the baptism I receive. But sitting on my right or left isn’t mine to assign; those places belong to the ones my Father prepared them for.”
When the other ten disciples heard, they were annoyed with the two brothers.
But Jesus called them over: “You know how rulers of the nations boss people around and their powerful people throw their weight around.
“It won’t be like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you must serve the others,
“and whoever wants to be first among you must become your slave.
“That’s how the Son of Man came—not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd followed Jesus.
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard Jesus was passing, they shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted even louder: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped, called them over, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said, “Lord, open our eyes.”
Jesus felt compassion for them and touched their eyes. Right away, they could see, and they followed him.
